definitions.explanation: The final stage or ultimate end of something, especially of the world, of life, or of a long process. Carries a weightier, often apocalyptic or terminal nuance than a simple ending.

examples.japanese: {世界|せかい}の{終末|しゅうまつ}を{描|えが}く。
examples.english: It depicts the end of the world.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{文明|ぶんめい}の{終末|しゅうまつ}を{テーマ|てーま}にしている。
examples.english: This film takes the demise of civilization as its theme.

examples.japanese: {終末|しゅうまつ}{医療|いりょう}では、{患者|かんじゃ}の{苦痛|くつう}を{和|やわ}らげることが{重視|じゅうし}される。
examples.english: In end-of-life care, easing the patient's suffering is given priority.

notes:
Refers to a grave or ultimate ending — of the world, of life, or of an era — not an everyday conclusion. A homophone of {週末|しゅうまつ} (weekend), distinguished only by context and kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {終末|しゅうまつ}{期|き}: terminal stage (e.g. of an illness)
- {終末|しゅうまつ}{医療|いりょう}: end-of-life (terminal) care
- {終末|しゅうまつ}{思想|しそう}: eschatology; apocalyptic thought
- {世界|せかい}の{終末|しゅうまつ}: the end of the world

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最後|さいご}: the last; the end — ordinary, neutral word for the final point.
- {終|お}わり: end; ending — the everyday word, without the grave nuance.
- {末期|まっき}: final period; terminal stage — the closing phase of an era or illness.
